mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep edging up while RESIDENTIAL eases, weekday circulation will increase and retail visits will rise within four weeks. The mechanism fails if commuting mobility stalls or reverses, because retail demand will not receive the footfall spillover.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week mean despite a further 2+ point rise in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS above its recent low acts as a weekend substitution signal: more outdoor social activity precedes more shopping trips in the following two weeks. The effect fails when PARKS stays depressed or only rebounds without broader mobility recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from its prior weekly mean after a three-week decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 14 days after PARKS posts a 5+ point weekly rebound from a low.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall together, it signals renewed access constraints or risk avoidance that suppresses discretionary retail within four weeks. The claim fails if both series weaken but retail activity still rises, implying retail is decoupled from commuting restrictions.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both drop below their current four-week average by at least 3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior four-week mean after simultaneous 3+ point drops in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in GROCERY_PHARM relative to RETAIL_REC indicates substitution toward necessities and away from discretionary spending, which predicts lower retail recreation over the next week. The mechanism fails if grocery demand rises without a corresponding retail slowdown.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds RETAIL_REC by 25 points or more
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or holds steady in the week after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds RETAIL_REC by 25+ points.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stay suppressed, residents are spending more time at home and making fewer discretionary outings, which drags retail activity down over four weeks. The effect fails when home-stay intensity does not translate into lower outside trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases relative to the prior four-week mean even though RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 and WORKPLACES stays below -20 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A local trough and rebound in PARKS followed by TRANSIT implies return-to-city movement from outdoor leisure, which should lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks. The mechanism fails if park recovery is not accompanied by transit recovery.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases for two consecutive weeks after PARKS posts a weekly low
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the 14 days after PARKS bottoms and TRANSIT rises for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, a renewed decline in TRANSIT is an early signal that discretionary outings will be cut, producing lower retail recreation over the next four weeks. The hypothesis fails if transit falls while retail stays unchanged or improves.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -35 after having been above -34
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower than the prior four-week mean within 28 days after TRANSIT crosses from above -34 to below -35.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM turns negative while WORKPLACES continues to improve, routine errand trips are being displaced by commuting, and retail purchases should strengthen over the next month. The effect fails if grocery weakness does not coincide with workplace recovery.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses below 0 while WORKPLACES improves by at least 2 points over the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week average after GROCERY_PHARM turns negative and WORKPLACES gains at least 2 points in the same week.
